The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. Job 01a15f3a-537b-7058-94cf-740ca6b28fd0 completed with counts {"00": 53, "11": 47} under measurement key "m".

The original circuit had two bugs.
1. It used QB25. Garnet only has qubits QB1 to QB20. I read the live dynamic architecture, and it lists only two cz partners for QB1: QB2 and QB4. I chose QB2.
2. It used "cx". cx is not a native IQM operation. Garnet only accepts prx, cz and measure. I rewrote the CNOT with native gates. I applied prx(angle=pi/2, phase=pi/2) to QB2, then cz on (QB2, QB1), then prx(angle=-pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2. These steps are a CNOT with QB1 as control and QB2 as target.

I kept the first prx on QB1 as it was. That gate puts QB1 into superposition. The final measure now reads both QB1 and QB2 under key "m". The fixed instructions are prx QB1 (pi/2, pi/2), prx QB2 (pi/2, pi/2), cz QB2-QB1, prx QB2 (-pi/2, pi/2), and measure QB1 and QB2 with key "m".

The mock only returned 00 and 11, which is what a Bell pair should give. The mock backend returns simulated results, so this run checks that the circuit is valid. It does not measure real hardware quality.

The scripts are /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_f3caa17a-2c4-15/run_bell_fix.py and /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_f3caa17a-2c4-15/fetch_counts.py. The first script crashed after the job finished, because iqm-client 35.0.3 has no result_counts method. I read the counts from the same job with get_job_measurement_counts and did not submit it again.
